channel.title: Nerdy3D
channel.description:
Hello, I'm Lucas!

I am a kid trying to learn about the world, and I love to design and create things!
I like to repair old stuff, and make stuff with my 3D printer.

Some project files: https://www.printables.com/@Nerdy3d_3493266

videos.desc: This is my model of the Antikythera Mechanism, made using Fusion 360, Tinkercad, and a few other free CAD's out there. This model took almost a year to make, due to the constant changing of the model so it can be fully 3D printed.

videos.t: Opensauce 2025 Behind the scenes | Part one (Load in)
videos.desc: This video was recorded literally today, and shows what stuff I saw at the convention center as it opened. I saw some cool creators, and met Quintin Flower who generously printed my picture and downloaded it to a REAL floppy disk. I might post tomorrow about the rest of the late arrival exhibitors as the OS exhibitor discord showed alot of people loaded in later in the day after I already left.

videos.t: Last day of Opensauce 2025 and cool other stuff (Part 3)
videos.desc:
Sticking my hands in tesla coils and flesh machines to determine my fate, and also exposing myself to a radioactive lazer…

Also this is a reupload because YouTube’s bots copyright striked me for the Michael Bay ending music and it got set on private lol

videos.t: Opensauce 2025 Part two (Day one before the event)
videos.desc: This was the first day of Opensauce 2025! I met some AWSOME people and saw some amazing projects! From flesh machines that predict your future, to sticking my hand through a radioactive lazer, this event was a life changing experience that I hope I can share some of with you guys. Thanks William and the team for creating an event where I can meet other nerds like myself and have a wonderful time.

videos.t: Stuff I got from Opensauce 2025 as an exhibitor
videos.desc: These where some cool stuff I got from the load in days and the preview party before the two visitor days. I got to check out almost the entire venue, and brought home some cool items and gadgets.

These are almost all the mechanical Iris’s I have ever made up untill 2024, as the past year I have been giving out my finest ones to teachers and friends for fun.
Most of these are hand cut from wood and cardboard, but the two largest ones where the first and only lazer cut things I have made in my life. (So far)

videos.t: Weekend Project vlog #1 | Murder Drones props and Tags
videos.desc: In this video I race to complete my murder drones weekend project before I don’t have any time left to finish my homework. If you enjoyed this video, then please leave a like so that the algorithm doesn’t deadpan my videos into oblivion again.

videos.t: First look of the Stargazer V5
videos.desc: I thought it would be nice to post my progress so far; I have finally finished the main assembly for prototype V4, and started assembly of a new Orrery. V5 is made of carbon fiber PLA and ABS. The gears are ABS, as carbon fiber is bad when printing gears. I also filmed this like 2 minutes ago in the middle of the night, so sorry for blotchy quality

videos.t: I made a bracelet out of human ☺️ ☺️ ☺️
videos.desc: Made this instead of doing homework which is due in ten minutes 🗿

I made a prosthietic out of scrap that can be moved by little string tendons! This originally was just going to be a video of me explaining muscle groups around the hand for my anatomy assignment, but I chose to do this because it is cooler :D Sadly tho, the mechanism broke after a few uses

videos.t: Bringing back to life a piece of 2000's tech for my 3D printer

videos.desc: My setup of 80's sound gear hooked up to my microcassette player. Please note that the this isn't the normal cassette player, it's a microcassette player that only fits cassetes about 1/4 the size of normal cassettes.
the lines that pop up later in the video are because the chip emanates radiation off of it

I made this skeleton out of old stuff I found from random places, like the eyes where made from a plastic ball I found on the side of the road, and the skull is made from coat hangers and used starbucks cup warmers. The whole skeleton is based on my own measurements, taken by myself to make sure the skeleton is somewhat proportionate to the average person.
